615.saw: Image 1: about 27 lines of Roman-numeral cipher (dar + lxxi style numerals with strokes/abbreviation marks, interspersed with some clear Spanish words e.g. names Diego de Soria, John de Santangel), docket "De los Reyes cifra sin fecha", old mark T.C.Y.2. Image 2: about 25 lines, same Roman-numeral cipher with a few plain words (Salvador Duarte, la compania). No decipherment written on either page. Spanish. 4 images total (664R-665V); only images 1-2 viewed.

625.saw: Image 1 (folio 43R, old mark T.C.Y.5): dense full page of about 38 lines of stroke-and-symbol cipher, heavy show-through from the verso, no clear words, no decipherment on the page. 4 images (43R-44V); only image 1 viewed (image 3 fetched, not viewed), so the English cover was not seen.
625.note: PARES title is Documento en cifra, PTR,LEG,54,13: the cipher matches the Paz no. 4715 description (cipher document, 2 leaves); the English cover not seen here, so the mapping is plausible, not proven.

725.saw: Image 1: Felipe IV letter of 2 Aug 1630, 14 lines of mixed digit/symbol cipher (digits plus letter-like signs). Images 35, 37: two facing pages of dense symbol-and-digit cipher about 25 lines each (D.213, letter of 6 Dec 1630 to the governor of Milan; description says sin descifrar); image 39 is its cover (Respuesta ... Milan), image 41 the docket of D.214 Copia de carta cifrada. No decipherment on the viewed pages; D.201 (Descifrado de D.200) exists per description, images 3-4 not viewed. Spanish.
725.note: PARES description: D.200 cipher (decipherment D.201), D.213 cipher sin descifrar, D.214 cipher copy sin descifrar. Image 41 only shows the docket; the D.214 cipher text itself probably image 40, not viewed.

726.frame: unit D.61-84: images 1-3 (D.61 and next); unit D.40-60: image 14 (D.42), SANTA CRUZ,C.51
726.saw: Unit D.61-84 (58 images): image 1 is the letter of D.61 (24 Jun 1632), Philip IV to Santa Cruz, about 28 lines of mixed sign/letter/digit cipher, no gloss; images 2-3 facing pages of further dense cipher (about 30 lines each). Unit D.40-60 (52 images): image 14 is D.42, letter of 26 Feb 1632, 14 lines of digit/symbol cipher with the royal signature, no gloss; images 5-8 are clear Spanish letters and image 16 (D.43) a clear page naming Aguirre Maranano (looks like the decipherment, not checked against D.42). PARES descriptions list many cifrada letters in both units (D.42, 44, 58, 60; D.61-63, 66, 73-77, 80); only the pages above viewed. Spanish.
726.note: PARES descriptions say Carta cifrada for the letters; the sin descifrar term is a word-match, not seen on these pages; D.43 clear page may be a decipherment.

727.saw: Five of the six units had cipher letters of Philip IV to Santa Cruz (SANTA CRUZ,C.51): D.107 (20 Aug 1634) about 18 lines of letter/digit/symbol cipher, no gloss; D.108 about 28 lines of symbol-and-digit cipher; D.134 (1635) about 21 lines of symbol/digit cipher; D.155-175 images 4-6 a long cipher (letters, signs, digits, three pages, ending with clear words and signature of Geronimo de Villanueva, 11 July 1635) with no gloss; D.176-197 images 8 and 10 two pages of dense letter/digit cipher; D.198-215 image 6 (D.200, 10 Nov 1635) 15 lines of dotted letter/digit cipher. The other pages seen in the units (covers, D.133 clear, images 3 and 9 of D.198-215) were clear. Unit D.85-105 (12877555) not opened; its description lists D.96, 99, 101 as cartas cifradas. PARES descriptions say cifrada for the letters; none of the viewed pages carries a decipherment. Spanish.

733.saw: All four images: a clear Spanish letter (Genova, Don Pedro de Mendoza, 24 Dec 1592) of about 25 lines, and a docket/address page; no cipher signs. PARES lists it as Descifrada de EST,LEG,1424,78, so this record is the decipherment (contemporary clear copy) of the cipher at 1424,78, not the cipher itself.
733.note: The cipher original is EST,LEG,1424,78 (a different PARES record, not opened here). The no descifrada hit is a word-match.

734.frame: images 1-3 of 52 (Carta cifrada no. 1, Manila 27 June 1780), FILIPINAS,915,N.7
734.saw: Image 1: Exmo Senor, a few clear words then lines of numeric code groups (3-4 digit numbers separated by dots, about 9 lines); image 2: about 11 lines of numeric groups; image 3: about 5 lines of groups, then Dios guarde a V.E. Manila 27 Jun 1780, signed Josef Basco y Vargas, addressed to Joseph Galvez. Image 4: docket/blank. No decipherment on these pages. PARES description says each cipher letter has a copia descifrada (later images, not viewed). Spanish numeric code.

729.frame: image 400 of 523 (f. 217, item 145, Badajoz 18 Oct 1580), SANTA CRUZ,C.47,D.2
729.saw: Open double page; right page headed El Rey, folio number 217 (another number struck out), Philip II to Santa Cruz, about 25 lines of clear Spanish with a block of about 7 lines of two-digit number groups (12 through 29, with dots/accent marks above some) in the first third, and some clear words interleaved at line ends (quo, podian, pa, los, les). The left page of the spread is the cover/address leaf with Por el Rey. I did not see a decipherment written on the visible area (the left margin of the right page was cut by the gutter, not inspected). Confirms Brackx cipher location. Image index found by probing 300 and 400 only; the PARES image labels are plain numbers, not folios.

728.frame: images 11-12 (D.11, copy of cipher letter to Cardinal Doria, 24 Feb 1625) of 48; SANTA CRUZ,C.49,D.6-26
728.saw: Image 11: first lines clear Spanish (Don Phelipe ... Muy Rdo en Xpo Padre Cardenal Doria, He recibido dos cartas), then about 40 lines of number-and-letter cipher (two-digit and three-digit groups, Roman numeral xi, some letters); image 12: about 38 more lines of the same, ending with clear words and date Madrid 24 de febrero de 1625; no decipherment on these pages. Image 13 is the docket (Copia de carta de S.M. al Cardenal Doria cifrada en 24 de Hebrero 1625); image 14 is D.12, a clear Spanish letter (Doria, Palermo) that sends the decipherments. PARES description: D.9 Carta cifrada with D.10 probable decipherment, D.11 cipher copy, D.13-14 copia descifrada. D.9 itself (images before 11) not viewed. Spanish.
728.note: The no descifrada hit is a word match; the unit has both ciphers and decipherments (D.10, D.13, D.14).

732.frame: image 48 (cipher) and image 51 (clear counterpart) of 71; FRIAS,C.81,D.105-137
732.saw: Image 48: letter headed El Rey, Marques de Caracena, about 28 lines of digit-group cipher (two-digit numbers and letter-like signs), stamped AHN Nobleza, plate mark Original deteriorado. Image 51: letter with the same opening Marques de Caracena in clear Spanish, about 20 lines, which reads as the contemporary translation (decipherment) of the cipher letter; I did not compare it word by word. Confirms Brackx.
732.note: Descifrada copy attached to the cipher letters; the no descifrada hit is a word match.

723.frame: all 20 images viewed; key material on images 12-14 (ESTADO,3130,Exp.4)
723.saw: Expediente of 20 images: covers (Interceptacion), covering oficios of 1811-12 (Gutierrez, Canga Arguelles, Espoz y Mina, Cuerpo Expedicionario) and an inventory of intercepted letters. No ciphertext. Image 12 is the Cuerpo Expedicionario oficio (Cadiz, 5 Sept 1811) sending the keys for the intercepted letters of Generals Girard and Joy; image 13 is a handwritten Alphabeto de la Cifra del General Joy (letters A-Z with number values, e.g. A=12.33, B=4, with a Nota that many are incomplete); image 14 continues with the sign list (Wellington, Nelson-type nulls etc.). Remaining pages are clear Spanish letters, a Spanish list of intercepted letters of Jose Bonaparte (1812) and a Sevilla post-office certificate.
723.note: Not a cipher document but holds a cipher key (Joy, and the Girard key text on image 12); the intercepted letters themselves are not in this file. The sin descifrar hit is a word match.
